steps.u: Plot soil moisture per field from the Parquet exports and flag fields that stayed below 20% for more than 3 days. Use pandas.

i.command: python -c "import pandas as pd; d=pd.read_parquet('exports/moisture.parquet'); print(d.dtypes); print(d.head(3))"

i.content:
import pandas as pd
d = pd.read_parquet('exports/moisture.parquet')
d['dry'] = d.moisture_pct < 20
d = d.sort_values(['field_id','ts'])
d['run'] = (d.dry != d.groupby('field_id').dry.shift()).cumsum()
runs = d[d.dry].groupby(['field_id','run']).ts.agg(['min','max'])
runs['days'] = (runs['max']-runs['min']).dt.total_seconds()/86400
print(runs[runs.days > 3])

steps.a: Two fields qualify, F-07 and F-11. Note I measured a run as first to last reading below 20%, so gaps from sensor outages inside a run are counted as dry. I haven't made the chart yet.

reference.summary: Wrote a pandas script that finds fields whose soil moisture stayed under 20% for more than three days, and found two, F-07 and F-11. Runs are measured first to last low reading, so sensor outage gaps inside a run count as dry. The per-field chart was not made yet.
